history.heading: Ancient Macedonia and Byzantine era
paragraphs: The region was home to the Paeonians and other peoples and lay on the northern edge of ancient Macedon, the kingdom of Philip II and Alexander the Great, whose heartland was in present-day Greece. It became part of the Roman and Byzantine empires. Slavs settled in the 6th and 7th centuries.

In the 9th century Saints Clement and Naum founded a famous literary school at Ohrid, which helped spread Slavic literacy. Ohrid, with its lake and many churches, is a UNESCO World Heritage Site. The region was part of the Bulgarian and Serbian medieval states.

history.heading: Ottoman rule and Yugoslavia
paragraphs: The Ottomans ruled the region for over five centuries. The Ilinden Uprising of 1903 against Ottoman rule became a national symbol. After the Balkan Wars of 1912–13, the region was divided among Serbia, Greece and Bulgaria.
After the Second World War, the People's Republic of Macedonia became a republic within socialist Yugoslavia, and the Macedonian language was codified.

history.heading: Independence
paragraphs: Macedonia declared independence peacefully in 1991. Greece objected to its name, arguing it implied claims on the Greek region of Macedonia. In 2001 an armed conflict between ethnic Albanian insurgents and security forces ended with the Ohrid Agreement, which expanded Albanian minority rights.
The 2018 Prespa Agreement with Greece renamed the country North Macedonia, allowing it to join NATO in 2020. EU accession has been delayed by disputes with Bulgaria over history and language.

culture.heading: Peoples and traditions
paragraphs: Macedonian, a South Slavic language written in Cyrillic, is the official language, and Albanian is co-official. Ethnic Macedonians, mostly Orthodox Christian, form the majority, and Albanians, mostly Muslim, make up about a quarter of the population.
Tavče gravče (baked beans) and ajvar (red pepper relish) are traditional dishes. Folk music features complex rhythms. Mother Teresa was born in Skopje.

politics.heading: Parliamentary republic
paragraphs: North Macedonia is a parliamentary republic. The centre-right VMRO-DPMNE and the Social Democrats are the main parties, and Albanian parties are usually part of governing coalitions. VMRO-DPMNE returned to power in 2024. A 2025 nightclub fire in Kočani that killed dozens sparked protests about corruption.

economy.heading: Economic structure
paragraphs: North Macedonia is an upper-middle-income economy. Key sectors include manufacturing in free economic zones (car parts and electronics), agriculture (tobacco, wine and vegetables), mining and services. Emigration and unemployment are challenges. The currency is the denar.
